newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Aid agencies, donors end inconclusive Zaire talks.
newsitem.headline: Aid agencies, donors end inconclusive Zaire talks.

text.p: European donors and Western aid agencies reacting to the worsening crisis in eastern Zaire have ended inconclusive talks in Geneva as the West scurries to put an end to the spreading conflict, diplomats said on Wednesday.

Diplomats said the closed-door meeting called on French initiative ended late on Tuesday with no decisions taken on how to help an estimated 500,000 Rwandan and Burundian Hutu refugees fleeing ethnic conflict in eastern Zaire.
"It was a very inconclusive meeting. It was a brainstorming session and didn't lead to any concrete suggestions," said one diplomat.
"As long as there is no ceasefire agreement, it is impossible to provide humanitarian aid in the area," he added.

The meeting was chaired by French Secretary of State for Emergency Humanitarian Action Xavier Emmanuelli and joined by Belgian State Secretary for Cooperation and Development Reginald Moreels and European diplomats in Geneva.

Officials from the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC), the U.N. refugee agency UNHCR and the U.N. food agency WFP were also present at the crisis talks held in the French diplomatic mission overlooking Lake Geneva.
U.S. and British diplomats were not invited.

Diplomats said the meeting discussed airlifts of food and humanitarian supplies to refugees and the possible creation of humanitarian corridors, but it was unclear how any of the actions discussed could be implemented.
Airlifts of humanitarian supplies were described as "an extremely expensive venture", they said.

Western aid agencies have pulled out of the two flashpoints of Bukavu and Uvira in the region because of insecurity. They have had vehicles looted by drunken Zairean troops. A U.N. food warehouse in Goma region further north was looted at the weekend and UNHCR says it has lost contact with 600,000 refugees and has requested satellite photos to trace them.
